summary: Documented the tested M5-S05 step (docs, owner metadata-builder, agent for this step is not build-doc-keeper, so Steps 1-9 apply, not the Step 10 compile run) -- the build-level package.xml (29 types, 56 members, version 67.0) and its deploy-order.md, the last step of this build (M3-S05 and M5-S02 stay blocked). Re-rendered PLAN.md/CLARIFICATIONS.md from plan.json before and after the status transition. Appended five decisions.md entries sourced from the step's own envelope (2026-09-12T12-16-22Z), step-tester's envelope (2026-09-12T12-28-47Z) and reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M5.md Run 3: D-M5S05-01 (F-43 closed -- the Apex now travels in a manifest, proven by a real manifest-mode dry run; plus the flywheel record for a step-tester playbook gap that is named, not yet closed, because this build has only one build-level manifest step), D-M5S05-02 (this manifest follows M3-S03's safe deploy sequence, one position off M5-S04's compiled order -- both named, neither silently picked), D-M5S05-03 (six org prerequisites from four milestone gates compiled into one release checklist, none expressible as a manifest member or a molecular test), D-M5S05-04 (four release-owner decisions -- rollbackOnError, testLevel, validation timing, the backout plan -- left open by design per the skill's own Questions-to-Ask table), D-M5S05-05 (the <version> split recorded, not reconciled: nine step manifests stay at 62.0, the build manifest ships at 67.0 per G3 decision 6, a plan-level api_version remains a planner v6 item). Wrote two workbook rows (workbook/99-other-configuration.md CWB-OTHER-042 for package.xml, CWB-OTHER-043 for deploy-order.md), both owned by metadata-builder, both source_req_id REQ-001-REQ-058 because the manifest and its note aggregate across the whole build rather than serving one requirement -- the same reading M5-S04's five compiled-document rows already use. Added no new traceability.md row -- the manifest mints no requirement, the same treatment M5-S04 received -- and instead added a 'Coverage note' section stating that every REQ artefact with a named artefact cell (REQ-001-REQ-054) is now, for the first time, carried by a named member of one build-level manifest rather than only by its own step's manifest, grounded in step-tester's whole-artefacts/-tree two-way check (56/56 members resolved, 62/62 deployable files covered, 0 missing either direction). Re-ran check_rtm.py --file traceability.md --manifest-dir artefacts --repo-root <repo> from the build directory: unchanged at 58 rows, 0 orphans, 0 errors, 4 warnings (the same four Draft-row coverage gaps on REQ-055-REQ-058). Set M5-S05 to documented via build_plan.py set-status.
confidence_rationale: Both artefacts this step produced (package.xml, deploy-order.md) got exactly one workbook row each, both rows carry a real (if aggregate) source_req_id and a stated verification path, and decisions.md now carries every item the runner asked to be recorded. Held at MEDIUM rather than HIGH on the Step 11 trigger 'an artefact could not be placed in a section without judgment': Step 7 reads 'one row per requirement the step serves', and a build-level manifest that aggregates every prior step's members serves no single requirement of its own -- the same reading M5-S04's compile run needed for its five documents, applied here to an ordinary per-step docs step by analogy rather than by an explicit AGENT.md branch for this shape. Secondarily, step-tester's own formal run on this same step flagged an ambiguous, playbook-gap finding (agents/step-tester/AGENT.md Step 3 has no carve-out for a build-level manifest step whose own directory holds no component files) that this run could name in decisions.md (D-M5S05-01) but could not close at the source, because this build has only one such step to prove a fix against.

process_observations.observation: F-43, open since the M4 gate ('no manifest in the build carries the Apex until M5-S05 is built'), is now closed by a real manifest-mode dry run over the whole build (reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M5.md Run 3: 60/60 components, 0 errors except the pre-existing F-28) rather than by a source-mode run that happens to include the same files.

The whole-artefacts/-tree two-way manifest check step-tester ran found zero inconsistencies over the entire build: all 56 named members resolve to a file and all 62 non-sibling deployable files resolve to exactly one member, with no wildcards anywhere in the build to mask a gap in either direction.

Six org prerequisites (F-28, F-39, F-44, F-41, F-51, G4 decision 9) and four release-owner decisions (rollbackOnError, testLevel, validation timing, the backout plan) are all compiled into deploy-order.md but remain open by design -- a tested, documented, build-level manifest carries no automated signal on any of the ten, and every one needs a named human to close it before a real deploy.

agents/step-tester/AGENT.md Step 3 has no explicit carve-out for a build-level manifest step whose own artefact directory holds no component files -- step-tester inferred the whole-tree reading from this step's own acceptance_tests[2] wording and from deploy-order.md's self-described method, and named the gap rather than let the inference pass silently. Recorded as D-M5S05-01, but not closed at the source: this build has exactly one build-level manifest step, so there is no second run to prove a playbook fix against.

deploy-order.md follows M3-S03's safe sequence (assignment/auto-response rules before Settings:Case) rather than M5-S04's compiled ten-slot order, which follows plan step order instead. Both are internally consistent and both are named (D-M5S05-02); neither this step's own molecular tests nor check_rtm.py adjudicates which a real deploy should follow.
Every M5 step is now documented or blocked (M3-S05, M5-S02 blocked by design; every other step documented) -- milestone-verifier can now run the M5 acceptance report.
